Moisture associated with the northern edge of Invest 99W continues to
impact Guam and Rota with trade wind showers with Tinian and Saipan 
staying dryer today. While there are currently no thunderstorms in
the vicinity, increasing wind shear, sufficient moisture, and a
developing 99W will allow for isolated thunderstorms tonight through
much of this week for the whole Marianas. Models are in agreement for
99W to develop near Yap and move into the Phillipine Sea. Therefore,
the main threat to the Marianas will be the potential for locally 
heavy rainfall as remnants of Invest 90W merge with outer bands of
99W that could be enhanced by the strong ongoing westerly wind 
burst. Rainfall totals will depend on the speed, strength, and track
of 99W. This situation remains uncertain and will be monitored 
closely. However, the potential for a tropical disturbance to impact
the region next week is very low.

Marine...
Buoy and altimetry data show a steady trade wind swell with combined
seas of 3 to 5 feet. Seas are expected to slowly increase starting 
Monday night with with the arrival of a longer period north swell 
mixing with the easterly trade wind swell. An additional southwest 
swell is expected to fill in Wednesday or Wednesday night and cause 
seas to potentially peak late next week. The size of this southwest 
swell is still highly uncertain and will depend on the speed, 
strength, and track of 99W. While seas are not currently expected to 
reach hazardous criteria, this situation will be monitored closely.

Tropical Systems...
A broad tropical disturbance, Invest 99W, remains a largely
disorganized system roughly centered near 6N142E. Currently, 99W
is still rated sub-low for development and does not have a clearly
defined center, but this disturbance is embedded within a developing
monsoon pattern, with some support for Invest 99W developing towards
midweek as it drift west-northwest towards towards Yap, potentially 
merging with neighboring vorticity centers within the developing 
monsoon pattern. A prominent westerly wind burst along the equator 
ushers in deep tropical moisture into the overall pattern and
continuing to provide ample support for the tropical disturbance.

Invest 90W has been closed by JTWC as visible satellite imagery 
shows low-level easterly flow and no defined circulation. Remnant
moisture from this system is expected to move west-northwest as an
open wave before potentially merging with 99W or the broader, 
monsoon pattern.

Eastern Micronesia...
The overall pattern has quieted down over the course of the day with
Invest 90W largely dissipated and no longer being monitored by JTWC.
The Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is truncated east of the 
region, around a broad tropical disturbance east of the Date Line. 
Afternoon visible satellite imagery shows scattered showers building 
back in across Pohnpei State due to a deepening trough. Meanwhile, 
patchier showers are seen across Kosrae and Majuro, along a few 
weak trade-wind troughs moving through the area. For Pohnpei, 
numerous showers are expected to build back in overnight with locally
heavy showers possible through Monday afternoon. Afterwards, periods
of scattered showers are expected across the region as a weak ITCZ
pattern sets back up across the region. 

Light to gentle winds continue over the next several days, with
occasional gusts to 25 kt near heavier showers that develop near
Pohnpei overnight and Monday. Overall sea state remains fairly steady
with combined seas of 4 to 6 feet across Pohnpei and Kosrae and up 
to 7 feet near Majuro. The arrival of minor north swell around

Western Micronesia...
Satellite imagery shows scattered showers across the region with 
numerous showers over Yap Proper. Altimetry shows combined seas 
between 4 and 6 feet. 

Palau remains in a lull while residing within the center a 
circulation embedded within the monsoon trough. As Invest 99W begins 
to lift northward, the monsoon tail to its south will setup near of 
over Palau. A monsoon surge is expected to develop within the 
monsoon tail later this week, bringing fresh to strong winds and 
heavy rainfall to Palau's coastal waters. Convection looks to ramp 
up near Palau on Tuesday with numerous showers expected across Palau 
through much of the week. 

Yap Proper is currently within a localized area of convergence on 
the north side of Invest 99W and the broader monsoon disturbance. 
Numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms are ongoing this 
afternoon across Yap and look to continue tonight. A slight decrease 
in showers activity is expected early this week before heavier
